You are helping reverse-engineer the pest grammar of a shell binary at /workspace/executable (nsh 0.4.2) by observing its parse-error messages ONLY.

HARD RULES: You may only RUN the binary and read its stdout/stderr. Never decompile/disassemble/objdump/strings/nm/readelf/gdb/strace/ltrace it. Never search the web or download source. Don't modify /workspace/executable. Scratch files go in /tmp.

BACKGROUND: `/workspace/executable -c '<snippet>'` prints, for a malformed snippet, a pest-formatted error on stderr and exits 255, e.g.

    nsh: parse error:  --> 1:6
      |
    1 | echo )
      |      ^---
      |
      = expected EOI, word, redirect_direction, heredoc, and_or_list_sep, or compound_list_sep

The "expected" list is the set of pest grammar rule names that were attempted at the furthest failure position, DEDUPLICATED and SORTED BY RULE ID, where rule IDs follow the order the rules are declared in the .pest grammar file (with the builtin `EOI` always id 0, hence always first).

YOUR TASK: determine a TOTAL ORDER over ALL rule names that the binary can ever report, consistent with every observed list.

Method:
1. Write a script that, for each of MANY hundreds of malformed snippets, extracts just the "expected ..." list into a normalized comma-separated line. Generate snippets that provoke failures in every corner of shell syntax: simple commands, args, assignments (a=, a=1 x=, local, export), quoting (unterminated ' " $' $" and backslash at EOF), all parameter expansion forms (${x, ${x:, ${x:-, ${#, ${x/, ${!, $, ${}), arithmetic ($(( , $((1, $((1+, $((x=, $(()), $[ ), command substitution ($( , `, unterminated), process substitution (<( >( ), redirections (> >> < <> >& <& 2> &> >| n>&, missing target, >&x), heredocs (<< <<- <<'E' plus missing marker/body), pipelines (| |& trailing), lists (&& || ! ; ;; & trailing), if/elif/else/fi partial forms, while/do/done, until, for (for, for i, for i in, for ((, for ((;;), for ((i=0, arithmetic-for bodies), case (case, case x, case x in, patterns, ;;), functions (f(, f(), f() {, function f, function f(), subshells and groups ( { with missing close, nested), tilde (~, ~x, ~+, a=~), globs (*, ?, [, [a), comments, line continuations, `local`, `export a=`, array-ish `a=(`, `a=(1`, `${a[0]}`, and anything else you can think of.
2. Collect every distinct list. Each list L = [r1 < r2 < ... < rk] gives pairwise ordering constraints.
3. Topologically sort all constraints into one total order. VERIFY the resulting order reproduces every observed list exactly (write a checker script that re-sorts each observed list by your derived order and compares to the observed string). Iterate until 100% of observed lists are reproduced, adding more probes to disambiguate rules whose relative order is still unconstrained.
4. Also record, for each rule name, evidence about WHAT it matches (from which snippets it is expected in, and from which snippets it successfully parses). E.g. `any_string_span` is probably the glob `*`, `any_char_span` probably `?`.

Known partial order already derived (verify, don't assume): EOI < var_name < username < word < escaped_char < unescaped_char < literal_span < tilde_span < any_string_span < any_char_span < command_span < proc_subst_direction < backtick_span < expr_span < param_ex_span < param_span < double_quoted_span < single_quoted_span < redirect_direction < heredoc < elif_part < else_part < and_or_list_sep < compound_list_sep. Also known: comp_op < assign_op < arith_op < factor_op < word; word < redirect_to_fd; var_name < arith_for_exprs; normal_newline < command; assign < command; command < compound_list_sep; initializer > single_quoted_span; literal_in_double_quoted_span > param_span.

DELIVERABLE: write /workspace/notes/02b-rule-order.md containing:
- The final total order as a numbered list (this is the inferred .pest declaration order).
- The full table of every distinct observed "expected" list with the snippet that produced it and the error position (line:col).
- Notes on what each rule appears to match.
- Any lists that could NOT be reconciled with a single total order (these would indicate my model is wrong - flag them loudly).
Keep the raw corpus + script in /tmp but ALSO append the full normalized corpus (snippet -> position -> expected list) to the notes file, since it is the regression-test oracle.

Your final reply: the total order as one line, plus <= 25 lines of notes on anomalies.

Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

"""Generate corpus 2: prefix x token cross product to force rule co-occurrence."""
import json

PREFIXES = [
    "", "echo ", "echo a ", "a=", "a=1 ", "local ", "local a=", "export ",
    "export a=", "return ", "exit ", "shift ", "break ", "readonly ",
    "echo $((", "echo $((1", "echo $((1+", "echo $((x", "echo $((x=",
    "echo $((-", "echo $((~", "echo $(( ", "echo $((1+2",
    "for ((", "for ((1", "for ((i", "for ((i=", "for ((i=0", "for ((i=0;",
    "for ((i=0;i<3", "for ((i=0;i<3;", "for ((i=0;i<3;i", "for ((;;",
    "for ", "for i ", "for i in ", "for i in a ", "for i in a; ",
    "[[ ", "[[ a ", "[[ a == ", "[ ", "[ a ",
    "echo ${", "echo ${x", "echo ${x:", "echo ${x:-", "echo ${#", "echo ${!",
    "echo ${a[", "echo ${a[0]", "echo \"", "echo \"a", "echo \"$", "echo '",
    "echo $'", "echo $\"", "echo $", "echo $(", "echo `", "echo <(", "echo >(",
    "if ", "if true ", "if true; ", "if true; then ", "if true; then echo a ",
    "if true; then echo a; ", "if true; then echo a; else ",
    "if true; then echo a; elif ", "while ", "while true; do ", "until ",
    "case ", "case x ", "case x in ", "case x in a", "case x in a) ",
    "case x in a) echo b", "f(", "f()", "f() ", "f() { ", "f() { echo a ",
    "function ", "function f ", "( ", "( echo a ", "{ ", "{ echo a ",
    "cat <<", "cat <<E ", "cat << ", "echo a | ", "echo a && ", "echo a ; ",
    "echo a & ", "! ", "time ", "echo a > ", "echo a >> ", "echo a < ",
    "echo a 2>", "echo a >&", "echo *", "echo ~", "echo [",
]

TOKENS = [
    "", " ", ")", "}", "]", ";", ";;", "&&", "||", "|", "|&", "&", "!",
    "<", ">", ">>", "<<", "<>", ">&", "<&", ">|", "$", "${", "$((", "$(",
    "`", "\"", "'", "$'", "$\"", "\\", "~", "~x", "*", "?", "[", "(", "((",
    "=", "==", "+", "-", "/", "%", "#", "1", "x", "x=", "in", "do", "then",
    "done", "fi", "esac", "else", "elif", "{", "\n", ",", ":", "@",
]

S = []
for p in PREFIXES:
    for t in TOKENS:
        s = p + t
        if s:
            S.append(s)

with open("/tmp/probe/corpus2.jsonl", "w") as f:
    seen = set()
    for s in S:
        if s in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(s)
        f.write(json.dumps(s) + "\n")
print(len(seen))
